title: Paid "task" work-from-home vs. contracted part-time work
summary: A coordinator offers part-time online work rating products or labelling data. In the fraud case, the recipient is paid a tiny amount for the first tasks, then told they must deposit money to unlock "premium" tasks with higher commission. In the legitimate case, the coordinator from TalentBridge explains a contracted annotation job paid monthly by the employer, with no deposit.

shared_setting.recipient_profile: a student or homemaker looking for part-time income; profile sampled at generation.
other_facts: Work: short online tasks, 2–3 hours a day from home.
Both conversations are chat messages. Turns are messages rather than spoken lines, so short replies are expected.

fraud.label_rationale: The "job" requires the worker to pay money in to continue earning. Earnings are shown on a dashboard but cannot be withdrawn until more is deposited.
fraud.caller_objective: Get increasing deposits from the recipient.
stable_facts: Earlier the recipient received a small credit of ₹150 for three "trial" tasks.
Premium tasks require a deposit of [AMOUNT_5] (₹1,000–₹5,000) to [UPI_ID_2].
The coordinator claims the deposit plus commission will be returned after the task set.

dialogue_plan.speaker: caller
dialogue_plan.act: Coordinator messages about the part-time work and the daily pay

dialogue_plan.speaker: caller
dialogue_plan.act: Coordinator reminds them the ₹150 for trial tasks was credited and says there is a higher-paying task set now

dialogue_plan.speaker: caller
dialogue_plan.act: Coordinator explains commission is higher on "premium" tasks

dialogue_plan.speaker: recipient
dialogue_plan.act: Recipient asks what they need to do

dialogue_plan.speaker: caller
dialogue_plan.act: Coordinator says they must first deposit [AMOUNT_5] to [UPI_ID_2] to unlock the premium set, refunded with commission

evidence.text: Coordinator tells the recipient to deposit [AMOUNT_5] to unlock the next task set
Coordinator says withdrawals are available only after the deposit task is completed

legitimate.label_rationale: The work is paid by the employer under a written contract; the worker pays nothing.
legitimate.caller_objective: Onboard the recipient onto a part-time annotation project.
stable_facts: A paid two-hour training task is part of onboarding.
Pay is monthly by bank transfer to the recipient's own account, after the recipient signs a contract sent by email.
The coordinator asks for the recipient's bank account number and IFSC for payroll, nothing else.

dialogue_plan.act: Coordinator says they will email the contract, need the account number and IFSC for salary, and that the recipient never pays anything

markers.text: Coordinator states there is no deposit or fee of any kind
Only account number and IFSC requested, for receiving pay

cooperative.fraud: Agrees to deposit and asks for payment details
cooperative.legitimate: Agrees and says they will share account details after reading the contract

clarifying.fraud: Asks why they must pay to do a job
clarifying.legitimate: Asks about working hours and whether it can be done on a phone

resistant.fraud: Says they will only do tasks that do not need money
resistant.legitimate: Says they want to read the contract before sharing any details

suspicious.fraud: Says this sounds like the task scams they have read about
suspicious.legitimate: Asks why the account number is needed and whether it is safe

fraud: coordinator claims the ₹150 proves it is real and recipient still declines.
legitimate: recipient declines. The legitimate coordinator answers a suspicious recipient by explaining that account number and IFSC can only be used to send money, and that no OTP or PIN will ever be asked.

caller_continuation_limits: The fraud coordinator may reduce the deposit, point to the earlier ₹150, or add urgency. They must not switch to asking for OTPs or remote access. The legitimate coordinator must not mention any payment by the recipient.

must_preserve: earlier ₹150 credit and deposit request in _F
contract, no-deposit statement, and account-number-only request in _L
may_vary: task type (product ratings, image labelling, text review)

ambiguities: Asking for a bank account number is not evidence of fraud: it appears only in _L.
A small real payment to the recipient (₹150) does not make _F legitimate. It is part of the fraud pattern.
Both cases start with unsolicited messages.

evidence_references.claim: Task-based job frauds pay a small commission first, then demand larger deposits (C10)
Withheld payouts pending further fees are a red flag (C11)
